top.title: Coventry girls volleyball sweeps Hale-Ray for second straight Class S title and 14th overall
top.description: Coventry girls volleyball team celebrates their 3-0 win over Hale-Ray to capture the Class S volleyball state championship Friday, November 20, 2026 at Bulkeley High School in Hartford. (Jim Shannon/Hearst Connecticut Media) HARTFORD - The Coventry High girls volleyball team has a lot of players who have state championship experience, be it on a volleyball or basketball court, a softball diamond, or a track. That experience helped the top-seeded Patriots on Friday against second-seeded Hale-Ray at Bulkeley High. Coventry swept Hale-Ray 3-0 to win a second straight Class S championship and the 14th in program history, all since 2003. Set scores were 25-17, 25-20, 25-19. Senior setter Teia Ransford, who had 36 assists, was named the most outstanding player. Coventry used the hitting of junior Hailey Mayo (15 kills), senior Tessa Young and others to take the state title. There was also the stellar defense of junior libero Aliza Sobol, who dug up a plethora of big hits from Hale-Ray. Coventry (23-3) and Hale-Ray (23-2) went back and forth early in the first set until Patriots senior Emma Weber stepped to the line. Six points later, the Patriots had an 11-5 lead. When a Mayo serve was not returned, Coventry took a 19-7 lead. Hale-Ray seniors Olivia Thiele and Fenway Jankowski each served an ace as the Noises attempted to claw back into the set. They got to within seven points on four separate occasions, but a Patriot block ended the set. The second set saw more back-and-forth play. The Patriots led most of the way, but never by more than four points until a Mayo kill made the score 20-15, and her tip two points later put the top seed ahead 21-16. Hale-Ray pulled within four points, 23-19, but a kill by junior Rowynn Myshrall got the lead to five again. Noises senior Reagan Bean smacked a kill to make it 24-20, but the second seed couldn't get the ball back over on the next point and the set ended. Hale-Ray never led by more than a single point in any of the three sets. In the third set, Coventry slowly built its lead out to four points, then five. Bean provided back-to-back points on a kill and a block for the Noises to get to within 17-14, then a Patriot hit into the net made it 17-15. From there, Coventry pulled away to claim its state championship. top.description: Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images The Miami Heat and Rockstar Games turned a regular NBA matchup into a living version of Grand Theft Auto VI. Fans did not just watch a game on Wednesday night; they walked inside the world of Vice City. The arena in Miami became the setting for the game’s global launch, blending basketball with video game culture in a way few sports teams have attempted. The Wednesday night “A Night in Vice City” takeover featured a full arena makeover to celebrate the global midnight launch of Grand Theft Auto VI and attracted a surge of first-time ticket buyers. Hardwood floors and concession stands transformed into the game’s iconic locations. The team unveiled a special court design that served as the centerpiece for the night. Fans could buy food from fictional restaurants like Burger Shot and Cluckin’ Bell, which were set up in specific sections of the arena. The effort to make the whole building feel like the game paid off immediately. More than an hour before tip-off, local reporter Will Manso shared footage on X of unprecedented concourse crowds, admitting via Yahoo Sports UK that he had never witnessed such packed lines. A New Audience Steps In The most surprising result was the crowd makeup. Most people buying tickets had never been to a Heat game before. Per the same outlet, 95 percent of customers inside the team store were new shoppers, and overseas orders accounted for over 30 percent of all sales. This crossover brought in a group of fans who usually buy video games, not basketball tickets. The merchandise sold out fast, but some items remain available for those who missed the rush. Currently, five Vice-themed hats are listed as in stock on the Miami Heat team store website. Options for the Court Culture x New Era 9Fifty Snapback are available in “Vice City,” “Vice City Logo,” “Vice City Billiards,” and “Vice City Goodtime State,” and are priced at $50, according to Yahoo Sports. Giannis Shines in the Spotlight While the game theme drew the crowds, the on-court action delivered a dominant win. Giannis Antetokounmpo scored 27 points in his first game against his former team, the Milwaukee Bucks. He also grabbed 14 rebounds and dished out 9 assists. Hot Hot Hoops notes that in his minutes, Miami outscored Milwaukee by 12 points during a performance where he missed a triple-double by just one assist. Bam Adebayo added 26 points, and Davion Mitchell scored 24 on efficient shooting. The Heat used this win to extend their streak to six straight victories. With a 9-6 overall record, they have won 9 of their last 11 games and trail the second-seeded Boston Celtics in the Eastern Conference by just 2.0 games, per Hot Hot Hoops. The blowout allowed coach Erik Spoelstra to rest his starters early, limiting Giannis’s minutes in the fourth quarter. top.title: At 7-2, Have the Bears Met or Exceeded Your Preseason Expectations?
top.description: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 4: Head Coach Ben Johnson of the Chicago Bears walks out to the field prior to the game against the New York Jets at Soldier Field on October 4, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chicago Bears have completed what Ben Johnson would refer to as “2 quarters” of the 2026 NFL season. Despite early adversity, they’ve managed to come away with only two losses so far – a mark that would be more impressive if they weren’t still sitting in 3rd place in their division. Still, the halfway point of the season presents us with a great opportunity to look back at the record predictions of a few of our WCG writers and evaluate just how close we each were to predicting this level of performance from the Bears. It also gives us a chance to look at our predictions for the remaining games and how confident we may now be feeling in those predictions. First, here’s the Bears’ remaining schedule: Week 11 – Nov. 22 vs. New Orleans Saints, noon on FOX Week 12 – Thanksgiving Day at Detroit Lions, noon on CBS Week 13 – Dec. 6 vs. Jacksonville Jaguars, noon on FOX Week 14 – Dec. 13 at Miami Dolphins, noon on CBS Week 15 – Dec. 19, Saturday at Buffalo Bills, 7:20 p.m. on CBS Week 16 – Christmas Day, Friday, Dec. 25 – vs. Green Bay Packers, noon on Netflix Week 17 – Jan. 3 vs. Detroit Lions, 3:25 p.m. on FOX Week 18 – Jan. 10 at Minnesota Vikings, TBD And here’s our look back… Donald Gooch: I had the Bears at 12-5 on the season, so if you project out their record over the next eight games based on the first nine, the expected record is between 11-6 and 12-5, so the Bears are on pace for what I expected before the season. I expect the Bears to meet, and perhaps exceed, my preseason prediction. Jacob Infante: My expectation was that the Bears would finish the year with a similar 11-6 record to what they had in 2025. Now, my expectations are higher, especially seeing their offensive improvement and after the addition of Jeffery Simmons to the defense. Their divisional schedule will be difficult to deal with, but my expectation is now that they’ll end the season with a 12-5 record. TJ Starman: My original prediction was for the Bears to end up 11-6. I was pretty accurate with my expectations for the first half of the season, though I did ultimately trade a predicted win in week 2 vs the Vikings for actual wins against both the Eagles and Seahawks. That said, I still expect 3 more losses in the next 8 games, which would put my adjusted prediction at 12-5. Josh Sunderbruch: I had the Bears at 10-6-1 and just barely making the playoffs in May, and I had guessed 6-3 at the bye, so they’ve beaten my expectations by one win so far. I can see them going 4-4 down the stretch, for 11-6, but I’d love for it to be 5-3 (for 12-5). Either way, I see them making the playoffs but losing out on hosting a home wildcard game due to a poor record against divisional foes.

top.title: Deadline acquisition Ray posts solid stretch with Friars
top.description: SAN DIEGO, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 7: Robbie Ray #38 of the San Diego Padres walks off the field in the fifth inning during Game Four of the National League Division Series against the Milwaukee Brewers at Petco Park on October 7, 2026 in San Diego, California. (Photo by Matt Thomas/San Diego Padres/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to our series grading every member of the San Diego Padres’ 40-man roster. The roster being evaluated is current as of Oct. 18, prior to the end of the World Series. Because of that, it will include players who will be free agents once the postseason concludes. Each player will be graded on their performance in the 2026 season, including the playoffs. That performance will be weighted based on how much time the player spent with the team (availability is the best ability). Robbie Ray It’s never been easy to determine just what kind of pitcher Robbie Ray is. The veteran right-hander owns a 3.90 career ERA with 1,874 strikeouts across 1,606 2/3 innings. He won the AL Cy Young Award in 2021 with the Toronto Blue Jays, but posted a 3.71 ERA the following season. Ray has finished two seasons with a sub-3.00 ERA and seven seasons with a sub-4.00 ERA. But he’s never managed to achieve the kind of consistency that teams look for in reliable pitching. Overall Grade: C+ When the Padres traded for Ray at the 2026 Trade Deadline, he was in the midst of a career renaissance. In the final year of his five-year, $115 million contract, Ray posted a 3.08 ERA in 122 2/3 innings with the San Francisco Giant before being traded to San Diego. The Friars gave up shortstop prospect Joniel Hernandez and top pitching prospect Miguel Mendez in order to acquire the veteran. That’s a tough pill to swallow when considering that Ray is a 34-year-old rental. Ray was solid down the stretch, but immediately began struggling with command. His 5.08 ERA was mostly due to an insanely high 1.53 WHIP. Ray walked 27 batters in a mere 43 innings with San Diego. Still, he provided value and bolstered the Padres’ rotation down the stretch, pitching in three quality starts (nine total starts). Ray was also quite good in the postseason for San Diego. Walker Buehler was expected to start Game 1 against the Milwaukee Brewers in the NLDS. Instead, he was placed on the paternity list last minute and Ray took his place as the Game 1 starter. He started off quite well, and kept the Friars in the game, surrendering two runs over 2 2/3 innings of work.

top.title: Saint Mark's secures another state soccer title
top.description: FREDERICA – Saint Mark’s spent the first half repelling frequent St. Andrew’s scoring chances while getting a few of its own that the Spartans couldn’t quite finish. When Brayden Wrinn scored twice a minute apart early in the second half, the Spartans’ state title quest was just about done. They still needed some solid defense, which Wrinn’s teammates expertly provided. But those two goals help up in a 2-0 win over St. Andrew’s in the DIAA Boys Soccer Tournament final at DE Turf. “I actually thought first half, credit to St. Andrew’s, I thought they took it to us,” Saint Mark’s coach Dan Swasey said. “They had a great game plan. They wanted it. They were a little more physical than we were.” Wrinn’s 51 st -minute strike off Caleb Nelson’s feed on a counter-attack soothed Saint Mark’s worries. When he put the ball in the back of the net again one minute later, the Spartans could taste the title. “We didn’t really look great in the second half,” Wrinn said. “We knew we had to make a change because that’s all we have left in the season. “Caleb plays me a perfect ball. Just tap in. It’s great.” No. 3-seeded Saint Mark's (14-4) won its second straight Division II title and the 13 th state boys soccer championship in school history. Soccer split into two divisions in 2013. The Spartans won 11 state soccer titles during a 16-year span from 1986 through 2001. “First half our guys didn’t have it,” said goalie Thomas Swasey, the coach’s son, who also delivered several powerful free kicks to create offensive opportunities. “I gotta keep us in the game when our guys don’t have it. “I know they’re gonna score one or two and if I keep it to zero I know we’re gonna win because they’re gonna score one or two, every game.” No. 4-seeeded St. Andrew's (14-4) fell in the Division II title game for the third time in six years. The Saints won their lone state soccer title in 1981 and also reached the 1984 final. Saint Mark’s defense handled the challenge St. Andrew’s provided with Swasey fronted by center backs Declan Sullivan and Dylan Solomon. Senior central defender Brandon Kemp was out with an injury suffered in a quarterfinal win over Brandywine and Solomon stepped in. “We got to halftime. I think we made some adjustments that worked for us,” coach Swasey said. “I think our boys came out a little more juiced, a little bit more fire. “Once we got that goal I think it opened up and gave us a little more confidence that we could do it. We’re a little beat up and I think we just needed that confidence that we could make that goal and get them going so that was a big one by Brayden Wrinn.” Contact Kevin Tresolini at ktresolini@delawareonline.com and follow on Twitter @kevintresolini. top.description: DORTMUND, GERMANY - NOVEMBER 4: Konstantinos Karetsas of Borussia Dortmund celebrates his goal with Fabio Silva, Felix Nmecha of Borussia Dortmund during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD4 match between Borussia Dortmund and Real Betis Balompie at BVB Stadion Dortmund on November 4, 2026 in Dortmund, Germany. (Photo by Vitalii Kliuiev/Getty Images) | Getty Images Borussia Dortmund have a chance to finish match-day 10 top of the table, and all they have to do is beat Borussia Mönchengladbach, the team that currently sits at the bottom of the Bundesliga table with an abysmal 1-1-7 record. If you don’t feel at least a smidgen of dread for tomorrow’s match after reading that statement, then you haven’t been a BVB fan for that long. Dortmund remain undefeated, but have drawn three of their last five league matches, so they could desperately use a win to start to build some momentum again. Meanwhile, Gladbach’s season has been a catastrophe, but their win and draw both came within the last three match-days, so there’s a chance they are starting to turn their season around. Player to Watch: Joe Scally In a season that has been shrouded in darkness, Scally has been pretty much the lone bright spot for Gladbach. The full-back/wing-back has three goals and two assists in nine matches for Die Fohlen, leading or tied for the lead in both categories. He’s fast, he presses very hard, and he is more than willing to bomb forward when the opportunity to present itself. I was able to watch Scally in-person when Gladbach visited Köln last month, and he stood out as the best player for the Foals by a wide margin. Predicted Lineup Prior to the break, the biggest question marks in the squad were Waldemar Anton and Serhou Guirassy, both with relatively minor muscle injuries. According to Ruhr Nachrichten , Anton should be set to return to the squad, but Guirassy still needs more time to recover. While he was unlikely to start anyway, the youngster Samuele Inacio has suffered a meniscus tear and will be out for several months. Fabio Silva has played well this season and in Serhou Guirassy’s absence, while Konstantinos Karetsas has been in good form and deserves to start. Meanwhile, the midfield trio of Joey Veerman, Felix Nmecha, and Jobe Bellingham has been excellent and needs to play. In the back four, I would be happy with either Ryerson or Gadou at right-back. top.title: RSM Classic weather forecast: Heavy rain, 35-mph wind gusts expected Saturday
top.description: If the players thought wet, cold and windy conditions were tough on Friday at the PGA Tour's RSM Classic , they are bracing for worse during Saturday’s third round on St. Simons Island, Ga. This picturesque corner of southern corner of the Peach State –halfway between Savannah and Jacksonville – turned downright nasty on Friday. "Some of the toughest stretch of golf I’ve ever had to pay,” said Michael Thorbjornsen, one of three co-leaders at the midway point at 9-under 133, who played alongside Brooks Koepka and Blades Brown. “You’d pay money on every tee box for a par.” That bad, huh? “On hole 1, I think Brooks, Blades and I hit our drives around 240 (yards) straight into the wind. That kind of shows what it was like out there,” he said. “I don't think I've ever hit a drive that short in my life condition-wise.” More: PGA Tour player's brutal finish could cost him his card — and 10 others who missed RSM Classic cut Saturday’s forecast has the low-pressure strengthening as it moves northward along the coast leading to “higher confidence for areas of heavy rain and windy conditions“ Saturday morning, according to Tour weatherman Stewart Williams. The rain will become more scattered in nature Saturday afternoon as the system lifts to the north. If that isn’t bad enough, north to northeast winds of 15-20 gusting to 35 mph will decrease slowly during the afternoon as the system pulls away as well. top.description: Las Vegas Raiders TE Brock Bowers. Getty The Las Vegas Raiders have been in a rut recently, losing six of their last seven games. A big reason for that has been a brutal schedule. They inked right-hander Troy Melton to a six-year contract extension that guarantees him $46.5 million with incentives and a club option for 2033 that could max out at $98 million over seven years. The hard-throwing right-hander will turn 26 years old in about two weeks. He has one year and 68 days of MLB service time currently, so this deal arrives as Melton was still five full seasons from free agency. Exchanging an extra year until free agency, and potentially two years if the Tigers use their club option, to guarantee himself at least $46.5 million is a pretty good deal for both sides. Melton wouldn’t have reached free agency until he was headed into his age 31 season, and with pitcher injuries being what they are, there’s always the risk that he wouldn’t be as valuable by that point in his career. top.title: Lagos renews campaign against open defecation
top.description: …Calls for improved sanitation, gender-sensitive toilet facilities By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos State Government has renewed its campaign for improved sanitation, proper hygiene practices and access to safe toilet facilities as part of efforts to eliminate open defecation and promote public health. The Special Adviser to the Governor on Environment, Olakunle Akodu, and the Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services, Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources, Tajudeen Gaji, made the call on Friday as the state joined the rest of the world to commemorate World Toilet Day at Alausa, Ikeja. The 2026 celebration was held under the theme, “Sanitation and Gender Equality.” Akodu said women and girls required toilet facilities that guaranteed adequate privacy, reliable water supply, handwashing stations and hygienic conditions. He noted that Lagos’ growing population, rapid urbanisation and expanding commercial activities had placed enormous pressure on existing sanitation infrastructure. According to him, addressing the challenges requires deliberate public policies, sustained capital investment, institutional discipline and collective civic responsibility. He said the state government recognised that a clean, resilient and sustainable environment must guarantee every resident access to safe, dignified and functional sanitation facilities. Earlier, Gaji, who was represented by the Director of Sanitation Services, Hassan Sanuth, said the commemoration underscored the importance of proper sanitation in preventing diseases, protecting public health and promoting a cleaner environment. He described access to safe toilets as more than a basic necessity, saying it was fundamental to human dignity and public health. Gaji said sanitation was closely linked to personal security, social equality and the fundamental right of every citizen to live in a healthy environment. He warned that inadequate access to safe and private toilet facilities could undermine people’s health, security, dignity, education and participation in economic and social activities. The permanent secretary therefore called for inclusive policies and investments that would address the sanitation needs of women, girls, persons with disabilities and other vulnerable groups. Sowore promised to introduce N100,000 grants per semester for students, saying the scheme would provide financial support without requiring repayment. He made the promise during a live session on his Facebook page, adding that students should not be burdened with debt while pursuing their education. He said, “The NELFUND that this government has put in place. First, our party is going to abolish NELFUND. We will turn it into grants.” He added that the policy would replace the existing student loan arrangement. He said, “We are going to give N100,000 per semester, which is N20,000 more than what they are getting now. For two semesters, you get N200,000 so that you can focus on your studies.” Sowore argued that Nigeria should avoid introducing a system that could leave graduates struggling with debt, particularly in a country where employment opportunities were limited. Citing his experience in the United States, where he said he spent 20 years, the AAC candidate described student loans as a source of financial hardship for many graduates. He said, “The biggest cause of depression in America is student loans. Where are you going to get the employment to pay back the loans? But the truth is that even the loans they are giving to them now, they are not paying back. So it just makes sense to turn it into grants.” Sowore said a student completing a four-year program would receive a total of N400,000 under the proposed arrangement, assuming two semesters per year. He described the amount as a reasonable investment in young Nigerians who would contribute decades of service to the country. The former presidential candidate also proposed scholarships for students with outstanding academic abilities, saying beneficiaries could be sponsored to study abroad. “Grants for anybody, whether… scholarships for people who show exemplary ability. We give you a scholarship; we send you abroad,” he said. He advocated increased government investment in education, citing China’s support for students studying abroad as an example of how countries could develop their education systems. Sowore blamed the decline in Nigeria’s education sector for several of the country’s challenges, arguing that investment in schools was essential to reducing poverty and developing human capital. He recalled that during his childhood, free education and community efforts to ensure school attendance made education a priority. The activist also cited the University College Hospital, Ibadan, as an example of Nigeria’s former standing in the health sector, saying members of foreign royal families previously travelled to the country for medical treatment. nigeria.title: Peter Obi Will Win 2027 Election, What Happened In 2023 Won’t Repeat Itself — Babachir Lawal
nigeria.description: A former Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF) and chieftain of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Babachir Lawal, has reiterated that the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, will win the 2027 general election, insisting that the circumstances surrounding the 2023 presidential poll will not be repeated. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Friday, Lawal predicted that Obi would emerge victorious, expressing the belief that the political dynamics of the next election would be different from those of 2023. ﻿ He also questioned the outcome of the 2023 presidential election, arguing that there should have been a runoff as Obi got the highest number of votes, a development he believes would have changed the political calculations surrounding the contest. “Peter got the majority of votes; he didn’t get the spread. Bola Tinubu got the spread and came second. There should have been a runoff in that election,” he maintained. The former SGF further projected that Obi would win Kogi, Benue and Plateau states, while defeating former Vice President Atiku Abubakar of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) in his home state of Adamawa. “I give it to you that Peter didn’t have more spread. This time, Peter will get the spread in Nigeria. “Atiku will come third in Adamawa State this time around,” he added. On the ADC candidate’s chances in the forthcoming election, Lawal argued that the former vice president would not have sufficient ethnic support to secure the presidency. Comparing the NDC ticket with those of other political parties, he described it as a better option. Lawal also disclosed that the party’s campaign strategy would prioritise town hall meetings, which he considers a more effective means of engaging voters. He said Nigerians would look in the direction of Obi due to his character and competence. “First of all, he is incorruptible. Second, he is detribalised. Third, he is a businessman that understands market forces. And fourth, he is a man who sticks to his words,” the NDC chieftain added. Asked whether the former Anambra State governor made any promises to him, the former SGF said, “No, he doesn’t need to”. The 72-year-old said he would go back to his 4,000 hectares of farmland where he produces cash crops and livestock, and watch Nigeria grow. Asked whether he does not want to partake in Obi’s government if he wins, Babachir said, “I’m 72 years old. I have a 40-year-old son. What is wrong if Peter says, ‘I’m going to make you Minister of Agric,’ and I say Peter, instead, give my son Minister of Agric. Is that wrong? In those days when we were young, that’s how things were done.” The post Peter Obi Will Win 2027 Election, What Happened In 2023 Won’t Repeat Itself — Babachir Lawal appeared first on Channels Television .

nigeria.title: [VIDEO] I Would’ve Advised El-Rufai To Talk Less If I Had Had Contact With Him — Yahaya Bello
nigeria.description: Former Kogi State Governor, Yahaya Bello, has said he would have advised former Kaduna State governor, Nasir El-Rufai, to speak less if he had had the opportunity to speak with him before his legal battle began. Bello, who spoke during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Friday, said he would have urged El-Rufai to talk less, remain in the All Progressives Congress (APC) that he helped build, and wait to see what President Bola Tinubu would do. He described El-Rufai as a respected and idealistic person who pursues whatever he believes in. Bello said that though he does not wish him “to go down the drain,” the embattled former Kaduna governor must have learnt how to handle political differences. El-Rufai is facing legal battles involving the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) and the Department of State Services (DSS), alongside allegations of financial misconduct and unlawful phone interception. In October, the Court of Appeal dismissed his appeal against the refusal of bail in the alleged financial misconduct case, upholding his continued detention by the ICPC. In a separate DSS prosecution over alleged unlawful interception of National Security Adviser Nuhu Ribadu’s telephone communications, the Federal High Court on October 26 dismissed his no-case submission and ordered him to enter his defence, adjourning proceedings to November 25. The Kaduna corruption trial, involving an alleged ₦8.68 billion CCTV contract, was adjourned to December 8, while a ₦1 billion fundamental rights suit against the ICPC, police and AGF is scheduled for judgment on December 2. nigeria.title: Oyedele urges banks to prioritise agricultural lending
nigeria.description: …Commissions Moniepoint Abuja branch By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, has urged banks and other financial institutions to make loans more affordable and accessible to businesses, particularly those operating in the agricultural sector, to stimulate productivity and economic growth. Oyedele made the call on Friday at the commissioning of the Abuja branch office of Moniepoint Microfinance Bank (MFB). He said access to affordable financing remained a major challenge for small businesses, stressing that interest rates, fees, repayment periods and the time required to secure loans must be considered in determining the usefulness of credit facilities. “We also must make business finance more affordable and more useful for many small businesses. The challenge is obtaining finance at a cost and on terms that they can sustain. “Affordability involves the interest rates, the fees that we charge, the repayment period, and time spent securing even that facility itself. All of these decide whether financing helps a business or puts it under strain,” he said. The minister said while the government had a responsibility to strengthen economic conditions to make financing more affordable, financial institutions must also contribute through efficient operations, improved risk assessment and transparent pricing. He particularly emphasised the need for increased lending to agriculture, noting that every segment of the value chain required adequate financial support. According to him, farmers need timely access to inputs and working capital, aggregators require funds to purchase produce, while processors need financing for equipment, storage and reliable supplies. He added that transporters and traders also required financial support to move agricultural products efficiently to consumers. Oyedele said appropriate financing for the sector would boost food production, reduce post-harvest losses, improve rural incomes and create employment opportunities. He, however, cautioned that agricultural lending must reflect the realities of farming, including production cycles, weather conditions and market risks. “Repayment schedules should follow production and harvest cycles. Lending decisions should recognise risks such as weather and market conditions, and partnerships with cooperatives, insurers, buyers and other credible participants can help lenders understand and manage them better,” he said. The minister urged Moniepoint to deepen its engagement with agricultural businesses and develop practical partnerships to support viable enterprises. nigeria.title: Tinubu focused on next generation, not next election, Owan-Enoh says
nigeria.description: …Targets APC victory in all 18 Cross River LGAs By Ike Uchechukwu, Calabar The Minister of State for Industry, Senator John Owan-Enoh, has said President Bola Tinubu is focused on building a prosperous future for Nigerians rather than seeking victory at the next election. Owan-Enoh stated this on Friday at Ikom Township Stadium during the inauguration of the Cross River chapter of Project Beyond’s executive and polling unit structures for the Central and Northern Senatorial Districts of the state. He described Tinubu as a pragmatic leader whose decisions were driven by long-term national development rather than immediate political considerations. The minister likened the President’s leadership approach to that of Singapore’s founding Prime Minister, Lee Kuan Yew, whom he credited with transforming the Asian country into a global success story. “That Prime Minister didn’t look at politics the same way a politician looks at the next election. That Prime Minister looked at the next generation. “That is what President Bola Tinubu is doing,” he said. Owan-Enoh acknowledged that the President’s economic reforms had subjected many Nigerians to hardship but described the sacrifices as temporary measures necessary for economic recovery. He likened the reforms to bitter medicine that would eventually restore the country’s economic health. “That tablet is bitter. But after that bitterness, you’ll get well,” he said. According to him, Nigeria has begun experiencing economic recovery and stability after three and a half years of the administration’s policies. He said the government’s next priority was to translate the gains into prosperity and improved purchasing power for Nigerians. “Three and a half years later, recovery has started. Stability has set in, and I think for President Tinubu, the next concentration is prosperity. “The next concentration is the power of your pocket,” he said. The minister further claimed that inflation had declined to about 14 per cent, expressing optimism that it would continue to fall towards single digits. He urged Cross River residents to support Tinubu’s re-election, arguing that the state needed to maintain its influence in national decision-making. “You will need to sit at the table when decisions are taken for you to be able to put before that table what you want,” he said. Owan-Enoh said securing the state’s political relevance required a strong electoral showing for the APC in the 2027 general elections. Recalling the 2023 presidential election, he said Tinubu won in seven of Cross River’s 18 local government areas. He, however, challenged party members to work towards securing victory in all 18 local government areas in the January 16, 2027 presidential election. “In 2023, out of 18 local governments, the President won seven. “In 2027, we must leave here with a determination and a resolve that, come January 16, 2027, Mr President is going to win 18 over 18 in Cross River, and that is possible,” he said. Represented by the Deputy Governor, Prince Kola Adewusi, at the Oja Oba Central mosque in Osogbo, the Governor recalled the struggles and battles for the sustenance of democracy in Osun State and vowed to continue to place the interest of the public at the heart of his administration. A statement issued by his spokesperson, Olawale Rasheed, on Friday stated that the governor commended Osun people for their steadfastness, perseverance and persistent solidarity during the electioneering period, saying the state has become a national model, a symbol for people’s power as the foundation of democracy. “I won’t disappoint Osun people. I will deliver even more than my first term. I am hopeful our financial situation will soon improve with the expected resolution of the local government crisis. We will take good care of workers and all segments of the society,” the governor was quoted as saying. Earlier in his sermon, Sheikh Moruf Ishola described the recent Osun election as “unprecedented in many respects and a standout record for all students of democracy. The call was made on Friday during the commemoration of the 2026 World Children’s Day at the UNICEF Lagos Office, with the theme, “My Day. My Rights. My Future.” UNICEF Chief of Field Office, Lagos, Celine Lafoucriere, said children’s rights were facing growing threats globally, stressing the need for governments and other stakeholders to guarantee every child access to education, healthcare, good nutrition, clean water, sanitation and social protection. “Children’s rights are under pressure, they’re under threat, they’re being increasingly threatened throughout the world,” she said. Lafoucriere said UNICEF was working closely with the Lagos State Government to ensure that children’s rights were respected and accessible to all, particularly the most vulnerable. She emphasised the importance of social protection programmes, noting that the existence of rights did not automatically translate into access to basic necessities. “Having a right is one thing, but it’s not going to put food on the table,” she said, explaining that social protection interventions could help vulnerable children access education, healthcare and adequate nutrition. She added that Nigeria’s future depended largely on the attention and investment devoted to children today. “The child is the future, and the future of Nigeria is today,” Lafoucriere declared. The Lagos State Commissioner for Youth and Social Development, Mobolaji Ogunlende, said the government remained committed to promoting the welfare, protection and development of every child but acknowledged that it could not achieve the objective without the support of other stakeholders. Ogunlende assured the children that their contributions and concerns raised during the celebration would not end with the event but would inform government policies and practical interventions. nigeria.title: Ooni urges FG to revive, protect textile industry
nigeria.description: …Calls for prioritisation of Nigerian fabrics, investment in local production By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo The Ooni of Ife, Oba Adeyeye Ogunwusi, has called on the Federal Government to revive and protect Nigeria’s textile industry as part of efforts to strengthen the nation’s economic growth and development. The monarch also urged textile unions to deploy all necessary measures to safeguard the industry and encourage the patronage of locally produced fabrics. Oba Ogunwusi, represented by Olori Aderonke Adeyeye, made the call on Friday at the 38th Annual National Education Conference of the National Union of Textile, Garment and Tailoring Workers of Nigeria (NUTGTWN) and the Nigeria Textile, Garment and Tailoring Employers’ Association in Ile-Ife, Osun State. Commending the unions for organising the conference to educate their members, the monarch said an informed labour union was essential to the survival of democracy and the development of the nation. He said stakeholders must work together to restore the country’s textile industry, revive moribund mills and make locally manufactured fabrics a source of national pride. “It is important for stakeholders to protect our industry. Let us prioritise our own fabrics. Let us revive our textile mills. Let us make Made in Nigeria a badge of pride, not an apology. “We must honour labour. Every tailor, every cutter, every employer deserves dignity, fair pay and respect. Labour is not servitude; labour is nation-building. “Let us raise a new generation. Teach them craft, teach them the business, teach them discipline. Do not let this knowledge die with us,” he said. The Ooni further stressed that the survival of democracy was closely linked to economic prosperity, respect for workers and the protection of local industries. “Democracy cannot stand on empty stomachs. It cannot stand where labour is not respected. It cannot stand where industry is allowed to die. A nation that abandons its artisans abandons its future,” he added. nigeria.title: I’m The Most Transparent, Vilified But I Shall Be Vindicated — Yahaya Bello
nigeria.description: Former Kogi State Governor, Yahaya Bello, has expressed confidence that he will eventually be vindicated over the allegations of financial misconduct levelled against him by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC). He also described himself as the most transparent individual. “I am the most transparent and the most vilified. But at the end of the day, I shall be vindicated,” Bello said on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Friday. ﻿ When asked to respond to allegations of financial mismanagement while in government, the former governor urged people in doubt to go to the state and ask questions about how resources were managed. He said he pities those who call him a thief. The former governor also described himself as a man who was blessed by God and able to meet his needs and those of his family members. Bello, who has consistently denied wrongdoing, is facing multiple cases instituted by the anti-graft agency over alleged misappropriation of public funds during his eight-year tenure as governor of the state. The EFCC Chairman, Ola Olukoyede, said in an interview with Channels Television in January 2026 that the commission had filed three cases against the former governor and fulfilled its mandate by investigating and prosecuting him. According to Olukoyede, the responsibility for determining Bello’s guilt rests with the judiciary. One of the cases involves a 16-count charge bordering on alleged criminal breach of trust and money laundering involving ₦110.4 billion. Bello, who was the governor from 2016 to 2024, is standing trial alongside two former state government officials. The Federal Government alleges that the defendants diverted state funds to acquire properties in highbrow areas of Abuja and Dubai, United Arab Emirates. Bello is also facing a separate 19-count charge involving an alleged ₦80.2 billion fraud and money laundering before the Federal High Court in Abuja. However, some prosecution witnesses have given evidence that has featured prominently in the proceedings. In February 2026, an EFCC witness, Olomotane Egoro, told the Federal High Court that Bello’s name did not appear as a beneficiary, signatory, or party to transactions involving some companies allegedly awarded local government contracts in Kogi State. Similarly, in March, another prosecution witness, Mahmoud Abdulazeez, maintained that Bello’s name was not linked to the transactions involving property documents tendered before the court. In June 2026, the 17th prosecution witness, Shehu Bala, also told the court during cross-examination that Bello was not involved in the property transactions under examination. nigeria.title: The Other Black Gold: Nigeria’s Coffee Sector Wants A Shot
nigeria.description: Richard Ali grew up with the aroma of coffee wafting through his house in central Nigeria as his father, an accountant, worked late into the night, drinking powdered, instant stuff from Maxwell House and Nescafé. It was not until years later, travelling on the other side of the continent, that Ali had a taste of “coffee, coffee — brewed coffee”. “I have to bring this to Nigeria,” he thought, and he started looking into importing beans from Rwanda. Ali later discovered he did not have to: coffee has been growing in Nigeria for more than 100 years. A wave of entrepreneurs in Africa’s most populous country are turning towards the oil-producing nation’s other black gold — an uphill task in a place full of tea and instant coffee, and little sense of homegrown java as a daily staple or part of a wider cultural patrimony. A general view of someone handling coffee beans in a plantation in the Gorongosa mountain range in Gorongosa on May 20, 2022. (Photo by Alfredo Zuniga / AFP) But roasters say they have found a market — and sense of national pride — to tap into, even if Nigeria’s beans are not well-known. “We need to grow more coffee, whether for the domestic market, which is expanding, or the global market, which is now considering Nigerian coffee,” Ali, founder of Tigray Coffee, which launched in 2021, said over a cup of Nigerian brew, light with slightly chocolatey notes. Agricultural Investments In Ethiopia, hundreds of years of cultivation have bound coffee to local culture, while Uganda and Ivory Coast have become modern export powerhouses. Nigeria produced 1,808 tonnes of beans in 2024, according to statistics from the UN’s Food and Agriculture Organisation — a paltry sum compared to Kenya’s 49,500 tonnes that same year. The first seeds hit the ground in Nigeria in the 19th century, after coffee was introduced by British colonists. The crop is notoriously fickle and can only grow in certain parts of the country. But there has also been a dearth of investment in agriculture, critics say, as the government instead became over-reliant on the oil sector for revenues. Experts have long called for a more diversified economy. The government agrees, at least in principle: in May, agriculture minister Abubakar Kyari announced federal investments in coffee production in Ondo State, calling it “a powerful economic crop” that could create jobs and “boost rural livelihoods”. ‘Never Imported Coffee’ At the opening of a new cafe in Lagos last month, Princess Adeyinka Tekenah paired a local brew not with croissants, but puff-puff, a staple street food snack of fried dough. “I have been in the business for 12 years, and I have never imported coffee,” the founder of Happy Coffee said. business.title: SEC Freezes Assets in $560 Million Crypto Trading Ponzi Scheme
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine SEC Freezes Assets in $560 Million Crypto Trading Ponzi Scheme The Securities and Exchange Commission has frozen the assets of Indianapolis-based Backward Hat Capital and its two co-founders, saying the firm ran a $560 million Ponzi scheme that told investors their money would be turned into crypto and used for AI-driven currency trading. The agency said Backward Hat, co-founders Phillip Williams and Devin Johnson, Johnson’s firm Traders Point Capital and Joseph Anderson raised the money from more than 2,000 investors starting in July 2022. A federal court granted a temporary restraining order, an asset freeze and expedited discovery to halt what the SEC called an ongoing scheme. Federal prosecutors in New York and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission brought parallel cases. The SEC and CFTC suits were filed in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Indiana, and the CFTC said the court has appointed Kevin B. Duff as temporary receiver to take control of the companies and the individual defendants’ assets. The pitch: crypto, AI and 6% a month According to the SEC’s complaint , Williams and Johnson sold limited partnership interests in private funds through a network of promoters, including to Williams’s former investment advisory clients. They promised a proprietary, “AI-driven” algorithm that supposedly returned at least 6% every month by trading foreign exchange. Investor money, the pitch went, would first be converted into a crypto asset and then used for that arbitrage. The complaint does not name bitcoin as the asset. It says about $109 million of the roughly $210 million raised from July 2022 to September 2025 was sent to the fund’s Coinbase account and converted. Of that, more than $56 million went to personal crypto accounts held by Williams, Johnson and a relief defendant, according to the complaint. About $40 million ended up on three platforms where some of it was used to trade other crypto assets, but little to no money was used to trade FX. After October 2025, the scheme raised about $350 million, and none of it was sent to Coinbase. Where the money went The SEC said the defendants made more than $250 million in Ponzi payments to earlier investors and moved more than $220 million to themselves. The money paid for exotic cars, expensive homes, private air travel and other businesses they owned, and helped feed Johnson’s gambling. Promoters took more than $50 million. Anderson is accused of producing fake financial reports, including at least two “audit reports” and a “quality of earnings” report from a supposedly independent firm. The SEC said the documents falsely claimed the returns had been verified against bank and brokerage records. business.title: Researchers Publish Security Analysis of Bitcoin’s Post-Quantum SHRINCS Proposal
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Researchers Publish Security Analysis of Bitcoin’s Post-Quantum SHRINCS Proposal Several researchers have published a 131-page security analysis of SHRINCS, a proposed post-quantum signature scheme for Bitcoin, and are asking the wider community to look for flaws in it. Researcher Mikhail Kudinov announced the first version Thursday in a thread on X, saying the paper reduces SHRINCS’ security to the properties of its underlying hash function. The analysis, dated Nov. 18, estimates classical security of 121.4 to 122.7 bits for SHRINCS, though those figures rest on assumptions that include three unproven conjectures. Kudinov said the work is not finished. The team is still working on a new analysis of a property called SM-DSPR, whose bound has so far been conjectured, and on tightening a reprogramming step and improving a bound against quantum attackers. How SHRINCS works SHRINCS is a hash-based scheme, meaning its security rests on hash functions rather than the elliptic curve math behind today’s Bitcoin signatures. It places two designs under one key: a stateful part built on FXMSS with WOTS+C, and a stateless fallback built on SLH-DSA. Because both use the same hash function, Kudinov said, the proof has to cover both. Signature size is the main cost. Under the draft proposal, stateful SHRINCS signatures run from 548 to 4,619 bytes, while the stateless fallback is 5,777 bytes. Schnorr signatures on Bitcoin today are 64 bytes, and ECDSA signatures typically come in around 71. Signatures take up scarce block space, so larger ones mean fewer transactions per block. The risk of a stateful signature The compact stateful path carries a danger. It relies on one-time keys, and if a wallet accidentally reuses one, an attacker can forge a signature for that address and steal the funds. Wallet software therefore has to track the state of every key. The stateless path avoids the problem, but at a much larger size. Jonas Nick, Blockstream’s director of research, told Isabel Foxen Duke, head of the MARA Foundation, on MARA Foundation TV that wallets must automatically fall back to the stateless path whenever a state counter could be compromised. “It needs to be impossible for the user to behave in a way that this catastrophic event happens,” he said. “Wallet developers need to deal with this stateful component correctly.” Nick also warned that heavy use of the larger signatures would weigh on the network. “We don’t know what the fee market will look like once we have these very big signatures,” he said. “And it’s not just the fee market, it’s also just fewer transactions fit into a block, meaning fewer people can use Bitcoin. You suggest buying food outside, and before you finish the sentence, someone reminds you that there’s rice at home. It is usually the end of the conversation. In Asali Africa’s new series, it is where the conversation starts. There’s Rice at Home is a cooking and conversation show from Asali Africa, the Lagos-based creative development agency, hosted by Chef Soliat Bada . In each episode, Soliat cooks one rice dish with a guest, and while the pot does its work, the two get into the kind of talk that usually happens around food: family, money and what success really looks like. Rice is the most ordinary thing in a Nigerian kitchen, and the show makes a good case that it doesn’t have to taste ordinary. Over five episodes, released every two weeks, the menu travels from Jamaica to Saudi Arabia, back home to Nigeria and on to Louisiana. You don’t just watch the food get made, either. The recipes are written up in full on Asali Africa’s website, with the ingredients and method laid out step by step, so you can watch Soliat cook a dish and then make it in your own kitchen. The season opens with Rice and Peas with Oxtail, the Jamaican Sunday staple of rice cooked in coconut milk with red kidney beans (the “peas”), served beside rich, slow-cooked oxtail. Soliat’s guest is Michael Famoroti , co-founder of Stears, and their conversation turns to family and black tax: the expectation that once you start earning, you start supporting the people who raised you. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. entertainment.description: Entertainment Week Africa (EWA) , the pan-African platform for the business of creativity, opens its fifth edition in Lagos tomorrow, Wednesday, 18 November. The programme runs until Saturday, 21 November, and brings together creators, executives, investors, policymakers and delegations from more than 18 African countries. This year’s theme, Five Years of Closing the Gap, reflects the purpose EWA was built around: connecting African talent with the capital, markets, skills and audiences it needs to grow. Since its first edition, EWA has welcomed more than 67,800 attendees. The 2025 edition alone recorded 28,683 pass-holders from over eight countries and 50 industries, across 61 sessions, 93 film screenings, 20 music showcases and nine fashion showcases. By day and by night The week runs across two venues. By day, EbonyLife Place on Victoria Island hosts panels, roundtables, workshops, masterclasses, and film screenings. By night, the programme moves to the Livespot Entertarium in Ikate, beginning with Opening Night on 18 November at 6pm, an evening of music, fashion, film, comedy and awards. The Entertarium also houses the week’s experiences, including an exhibition, the EWA Art Floor, a fashion show, comedy, live music, a beauty exhibition and a marketplace. Seven tracks, one market The 2026 programme is organised across seven tracks: Film & TV; Music; Fashion & Beauty; AI & Tech; Live Events & Production; Creative Enterprise; and Art & Animation, which is new this year. Alongside the conference, EWA runs a set of commercial formats designed to move deals forward. They include the EWA Deal Room, the Content and Music Markets, the EWA Capital Desk, the Creators Hub and LABSPOT, EWA’s skills and enterprise development engine. Last year’s Deal Room received more than 178 entries and advanced nine companies to its accelerator, with Future Africa, Catalyst Fund, Consonance Invest and Askya Investment Partners among the participating investors and partners. Between 30 and 40 per cent of this year’s delegates are expected to travel from outside Nigeria, with delegations from Kenya, Rwanda, Ghana, Senegal, Uganda, Tanzania and South Africa among them. The edition will also host the exclusive screening of University of Side Hustle, the first scripted feature film from Livespot Studios, written by Dami Elebe , executive produced by Deola Art Alade. The road to Lagos The fifth edition follows a year in which EWA took its conversation abroad through EWA Creative Connect, its invitation-only convenings. The first was held in Los Angeles during Grammy Week, with executives from Warner Records, Adobe, Amazon and Unilever among the participants. The second took place in London during the Nigeria–UK state visit, with the British Film Institute, Diageo and the Ministry of Trade and Investment in attendance. entertainment.title: Visa Report Identifies Opportunity to Integrate Digital Payments with SMEs Business Operations in Nigeria
entertainment.description: Report identifies next SME digitization opportunity: connecting payments with day-to-day business management. 94% of SMEs surveyed find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, yet only 29% currently use one, pointing to untapped demand for tools that connect payments with business management. Integrated payment and business solutions can give financial institutions a more holistic view of SME cash flow and support more tailored financing solutions over time. Small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria have largely moved beyond the first stage of digital payment adoption, but a productivity gap remains. According to Visa’s new survey for its Pay and Get Paid 2026 report, most of the SMEs surveyed in Nigeria use digital payments, showing how firmly digital commerce has taken root in the country’s small business economy. However, many SMEs still manage the related financial and operational tasks separately, with only 29% currently using an integrated solution that connects payments with broader business management. The report shows that financial admin and disconnected tools create friction for SMEs, with surveyed businesses citing challenges in tracking outstanding invoices (14%), keeping payroll records organized (19%), and preparing financial reports (16%). These pain points reflect a disconnect between payments and the operational tasks that follow, with some businesses juggling multiple systems to keep their business running. The appetite for a more connected approach is clear. According to the report, 94% of SMEs find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, reflecting strong interest in tools that can bring payments and key business operations into one experience. However, adoption has yet to catch up: only 29% of SMEs currently use an integrated payment and business platform. The report points to several perception barriers that may be slowing adoption. Businesses cited that they already have manual processes that work (8%), that an integrated platform may disrupt their current way of working (8%), or that they do not trust relying on a single provider (7%). These findings suggest that broader adoption will depend on helping SMEs better understand how integrated tools can be relevant, accessible, and scalable for businesses at different stages of growth. At the same time, the experience of SMEs already using integrated solutions suggests a strong value case. The report found that Nigerian businesses using an integrated tool or platform report 93% satisfaction, with 88% reporting efficiency gains, including reductions in the time and effort required to manage their business. Beyond efficiency, integrated platforms may also create new opportunities for financial institutions to deepen SME relationships by using richer payments and business-management data to better understand cash flow patterns, support risk assessment, and potentially enable more relevant lending solutions over time. Andrew Uaboi , Vice

entertainment.title: Fela Anikulapo-Kuti and Sade Adu Make History With 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Inductions
entertainment.description: Sade Adu in the Performer category and Fela Kuti in the Early Influence category, both inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Class of 2026. Nigerian music history just added another major chapter in Los Angeles, and the celebration has been loud from Lagos to London. On Saturday, 14 November 2026, Afrobeat pioneer Fela Aníkúlápó Kuti and Nigerian-British singer Sade Adu were officially inducted into the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame during a star-studded ceremony at the Peacock Theatre. For Fela Kuti, nearly three decades after his passing in 1997, this induction makes him the first African-born solo artist to enter the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame. Honoured posthumously in the Early Influence category—five years after he was first nominated in 2021—the recognition celebrates how he fused West African rhythms with jazz, funk, and soul to create Afrobeat, using his voice and horns to confront social and political injustice across classics like “Zombie”, “Water No Get Enemy”, and “Sorrow, Tears and Blood”. It also caps off an extraordinary 2026 for his legacy, coming just months after the Recording Academy presented him with a posthumous Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award in February, another first for an African artist. From left, Made Kuti, Femi Kuti, Yeni Kuti, and Seun Kuti in Los Angeles for Fela Aníkúlápó Kuti’s posthumous induction into the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame. Photo Credit: Femi Kuti/Instagram Representing the Afrobeat legend on the night were members of the Kuti family, with his children Yeni Kuti , Femi Kuti , Seun Kuti , and Shalewa Kuti , alongside his grandson Made Kuti , stepping out in Los Angeles to accept the honour on his behalf. Speaking on the milestone, the family reflected on how remarkable it is to see Fela receive both the Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award and a Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction in the very same year. Meanwhile, Sade Adu —born Helen Folasade Adu in Ibadan—was inducted in th e Performer category as the frontwoman of her acclaimed British band Sade , alongside longtime bandmates Stuart Matthewman , Paul Spencer Denman , and Andrew Hale . Earning their spot on their second nomination, the group behind timeless soul-jazz records such as “Smooth Operator”, “The Sweetest Taboo”, and “Your Love Is King” opted to sit out the ceremony in true low-key fashion, though they shared a warm message thanking fans and dedicating the milestone to their late longtime producer Mike Pela . From left, Seun Kuti, Yeni Kuti, Femi Kuti, Shalewa Kuti, and Made Kuti arrive on the red carpet at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles for Fela Aníkúlápó Kuti’s posthumous induction into the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame. sports.title: Coventry girls volleyball sweeps Hale-Ray for second straight Class S title and 14th overall
sports.description: Coventry girls volleyball team celebrates their 3-0 win over Hale-Ray to capture the Class S volleyball state championship Friday, November 20, 2026 at Bulkeley High School in Hartford. (Jim Shannon/Hearst Connecticut Media) HARTFORD - The Coventry High girls volleyball team has a lot of players who have state championship experience, be it on a volleyball or basketball court, a softball diamond, or a track. That experience helped the top-seeded Patriots on Friday against second-seeded Hale-Ray at Bulkeley High. Coventry swept Hale-Ray 3-0 to win a second straight Class S championship and the 14th in program history, all since 2003. Set scores were 25-17, 25-20, 25-19. Senior setter Teia Ransford, who had 36 assists, was named the most outstanding player. Coventry used the hitting of junior Hailey Mayo (15 kills), senior Tessa Young and others to take the state title. There was also the stellar defense of junior libero Aliza Sobol, who dug up a plethora of big hits from Hale-Ray. Coventry (23-3) and Hale-Ray (23-2) went back and forth early in the first set until Patriots senior Emma Weber stepped to the line. Six points later, the Patriots had an 11-5 lead. When a Mayo serve was not returned, Coventry took a 19-7 lead. Hale-Ray seniors Olivia Thiele and Fenway Jankowski each served an ace as the Noises attempted to claw back into the set. They got to within seven points on four separate occasions, but a Patriot block ended the set. The second set saw more back-and-forth play. The Patriots led most of the way, but never by more than four points until a Mayo kill made the score 20-15, and her tip two points later put the top seed ahead 21-16. Hale-Ray pulled within four points, 23-19, but a kill by junior Rowynn Myshrall got the lead to five again. Noises senior Reagan Bean smacked a kill to make it 24-20, but the second seed couldn't get the ball back over on the next point and the set ended. Hale-Ray never led by more than a single point in any of the three sets. In the third set, Coventry slowly built its lead out to four points, then five. Bean provided back-to-back points on a kill and a block for the Noises to get to within 17-14, then a Patriot hit into the net made it 17-15. From there, Coventry pulled away to claim its state championship. sports.title: Miami Heat GTA 6 Night Draws Record Fans And Massive Sales
sports.description: Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images The Miami Heat and Rockstar Games turned a regular NBA matchup into a living version of Grand Theft Auto VI. Fans did not just watch a game on Wednesday night; they walked inside the world of Vice City. The arena in Miami became the setting for the game’s global launch, blending basketball with video game culture in a way few sports teams have attempted. The Wednesday night “A Night in Vice City” takeover featured a full arena makeover to celebrate the global midnight launch of Grand Theft Auto VI and attracted a surge of first-time ticket buyers. Hardwood floors and concession stands transformed into the game’s iconic locations. The team unveiled a special court design that served as the centerpiece for the night. Fans could buy food from fictional restaurants like Burger Shot and Cluckin’ Bell, which were set up in specific sections of the arena. The effort to make the whole building feel like the game paid off immediately. More than an hour before tip-off, local reporter Will Manso shared footage on X of unprecedented concourse crowds, admitting via Yahoo Sports UK that he had never witnessed such packed lines. A New Audience Steps In The most surprising result was the crowd makeup. Most people buying tickets had never been to a Heat game before. Per the same outlet, 95 percent of customers inside the team store were new shoppers, and overseas orders accounted for over 30 percent of all sales. This crossover brought in a group of fans who usually buy video games, not basketball tickets. The merchandise sold out fast, but some items remain available for those who missed the rush. Currently, five Vice-themed hats are listed as in stock on the Miami Heat team store website. Options for the Court Culture x New Era 9Fifty Snapback are available in “Vice City,” “Vice City Logo,” “Vice City Billiards,” and “Vice City Goodtime State,” and are priced at $50, according to Yahoo Sports. Giannis Shines in the Spotlight While the game theme drew the crowds, the on-court action delivered a dominant win. Giannis Antetokounmpo scored 27 points in his first game against his former team, the Milwaukee Bucks. He also grabbed 14 rebounds and dished out 9 assists. Hot Hot Hoops notes that in his minutes, Miami outscored Milwaukee by 12 points during a performance where he missed a triple-double by just one assist. Bam Adebayo added 26 points, and Davion Mitchell scored 24 on efficient shooting. The Heat used this win to extend their streak to six straight victories. With a 9-6 overall record, they have won 9 of their last 11 games and trail the second-seeded Boston Celtics in the Eastern Conference by just 2.0 games, per Hot Hot Hoops. The blowout allowed coach Erik Spoelstra to rest his starters early, limiting Giannis’s minutes in the fourth quarter. sports.title: At 7-2, Have the Bears Met or Exceeded Your Preseason Expectations?
sports.description: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 4: Head Coach Ben Johnson of the Chicago Bears walks out to the field prior to the game against the New York Jets at Soldier Field on October 4, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chicago Bears have completed what Ben Johnson would refer to as “2 quarters” of the 2026 NFL season. Despite early adversity, they’ve managed to come away with only two losses so far – a mark that would be more impressive if they weren’t still sitting in 3rd place in their division. Still, the halfway point of the season presents us with a great opportunity to look back at the record predictions of a few of our WCG writers and evaluate just how close we each were to predicting this level of performance from the Bears. It also gives us a chance to look at our predictions for the remaining games and how confident we may now be feeling in those predictions. First, here’s the Bears’ remaining schedule: Week 11 – Nov. 22 vs. New Orleans Saints, noon on FOX Week 12 – Thanksgiving Day at Detroit Lions, noon on CBS Week 13 – Dec. 6 vs. Jacksonville Jaguars, noon on FOX Week 14 – Dec. 13 at Miami Dolphins, noon on CBS Week 15 – Dec. 19, Saturday at Buffalo Bills, 7:20 p.m. on CBS Week 16 – Christmas Day, Friday, Dec. 25 – vs. Green Bay Packers, noon on Netflix Week 17 – Jan. 3 vs. Detroit Lions, 3:25 p.m. on FOX Week 18 – Jan. 10 at Minnesota Vikings, TBD And here’s our look back… Donald Gooch: I had the Bears at 12-5 on the season, so if you project out their record over the next eight games based on the first nine, the expected record is between 11-6 and 12-5, so the Bears are on pace for what I expected before the season. I expect the Bears to meet, and perhaps exceed, my preseason prediction. Jacob Infante: My expectation was that the Bears would finish the year with a similar 11-6 record to what they had in 2025. Now, my expectations are higher, especially seeing their offensive improvement and after the addition of Jeffery Simmons to the defense. Their divisional schedule will be difficult to deal with, but my expectation is now that they’ll end the season with a 12-5 record. TJ Starman: My original prediction was for the Bears to end up 11-6. I was pretty accurate with my expectations for the first half of the season, though I did ultimately trade a predicted win in week 2 vs the Vikings for actual wins against both the Eagles and Seahawks. That said, I still expect 3 more losses in the next 8 games, which would put my adjusted prediction at 12-5. Josh Sunderbruch: I had the Bears at 10-6-1 and just barely making the playoffs in May, and I had guessed 6-3 at the bye, so they’ve beaten my expectations by one win so far. I can see them going 4-4 down the stretch, for 11-6, but I’d love for it to be 5-3 (for 12-5). Either way, I see them making the playoffs but losing out on hosting a home wildcard game due to a poor record against divisional foes.

sports.title: Deadline acquisition Ray posts solid stretch with Friars
sports.description: SAN DIEGO, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 7: Robbie Ray #38 of the San Diego Padres walks off the field in the fifth inning during Game Four of the National League Division Series against the Milwaukee Brewers at Petco Park on October 7, 2026 in San Diego, California. (Photo by Matt Thomas/San Diego Padres/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to our series grading every member of the San Diego Padres’ 40-man roster. The roster being evaluated is current as of Oct. 18, prior to the end of the World Series. Because of that, it will include players who will be free agents once the postseason concludes. Each player will be graded on their performance in the 2026 season, including the playoffs. That performance will be weighted based on how much time the player spent with the team (availability is the best ability). Robbie Ray It’s never been easy to determine just what kind of pitcher Robbie Ray is. The veteran right-hander owns a 3.90 career ERA with 1,874 strikeouts across 1,606 2/3 innings. He won the AL Cy Young Award in 2021 with the Toronto Blue Jays, but posted a 3.71 ERA the following season. Ray has finished two seasons with a sub-3.00 ERA and seven seasons with a sub-4.00 ERA. But he’s never managed to achieve the kind of consistency that teams look for in reliable pitching. Overall Grade: C+ When the Padres traded for Ray at the 2026 Trade Deadline, he was in the midst of a career renaissance. In the final year of his five-year, $115 million contract, Ray posted a 3.08 ERA in 122 2/3 innings with the San Francisco Giant before being traded to San Diego. The Friars gave up shortstop prospect Joniel Hernandez and top pitching prospect Miguel Mendez in order to acquire the veteran. That’s a tough pill to swallow when considering that Ray is a 34-year-old rental. Ray was solid down the stretch, but immediately began struggling with command. His 5.08 ERA was mostly due to an insanely high 1.53 WHIP. Ray walked 27 batters in a mere 43 innings with San Diego. Still, he provided value and bolstered the Padres’ rotation down the stretch, pitching in three quality starts (nine total starts). Ray was also quite good in the postseason for San Diego. Walker Buehler was expected to start Game 1 against the Milwaukee Brewers in the NLDS. Instead, he was placed on the paternity list last minute and Ray took his place as the Game 1 starter. He started off quite well, and kept the Friars in the game, surrendering two runs over 2 2/3 innings of work.

sports.title: Saint Mark's secures another state soccer title
sports.description: FREDERICA – Saint Mark’s spent the first half repelling frequent St. Andrew’s scoring chances while getting a few of its own that the Spartans couldn’t quite finish. When Brayden Wrinn scored twice a minute apart early in the second half, the Spartans’ state title quest was just about done. They still needed some solid defense, which Wrinn’s teammates expertly provided. But those two goals help up in a 2-0 win over St. Andrew’s in the DIAA Boys Soccer Tournament final at DE Turf. “I actually thought first half, credit to St. Andrew’s, I thought they took it to us,” Saint Mark’s coach Dan Swasey said. “They had a great game plan. They wanted it. They were a little more physical than we were.” Wrinn’s 51 st -minute strike off Caleb Nelson’s feed on a counter-attack soothed Saint Mark’s worries. When he put the ball in the back of the net again one minute later, the Spartans could taste the title. “We didn’t really look great in the second half,” Wrinn said. “We knew we had to make a change because that’s all we have left in the season. “Caleb plays me a perfect ball. Just tap in. It’s great.” No. 3-seeded Saint Mark's (14-4) won its second straight Division II title and the 13 th state boys soccer championship in school history. Soccer split into two divisions in 2013. The Spartans won 11 state soccer titles during a 16-year span from 1986 through 2001. “First half our guys didn’t have it,” said goalie Thomas Swasey, the coach’s son, who also delivered several powerful free kicks to create offensive opportunities. “I gotta keep us in the game when our guys don’t have it. “I know they’re gonna score one or two and if I keep it to zero I know we’re gonna win because they’re gonna score one or two, every game.” No. 4-seeeded St. Andrew's (14-4) fell in the Division II title game for the third time in six years. The Saints won their lone state soccer title in 1981 and also reached the 1984 final. Saint Mark’s defense handled the challenge St. Andrew’s provided with Swasey fronted by center backs Declan Sullivan and Dylan Solomon. Senior central defender Brandon Kemp was out with an injury suffered in a quarterfinal win over Brandywine and Solomon stepped in. “We got to halftime. sports.title: Raiders TE Brock Bowers Breaks Silence on Injury Ahead of Broncos Game
sports.description: Las Vegas Raiders TE Brock Bowers. Getty The Las Vegas Raiders have been in a rut recently, losing six of their last seven games. A big reason for that has been a brutal schedule. sports.description: Las Vegas Raiders owner Mark Davis has “a million WTF moments in a day,” and the latest one is thanks to Prime Video’s “Madden,” he told USA TODAY Sports over the phone Friday in the aftermath of the film’s release. Davis said he was “hurt” by the depiction of his father, the late Al Davis – a Pro Football Hall of Fame executive and coach best known as the long-time owner, general manager and head coach of the Raiders. It's12 just unfair. I don't know what the purpose of the movie was to be real honest.” Before the film was released Nov. 18, Davis said the filmmakers reached out to him about certain aspects of the narrative. When he screened the final product two weeks before its release, Davis said he was shocked by a moment that hadn't previously been mentioned. The moment happens in the aftermath of the 1978 preseason game where Raiders safety Jack Tatum delivered a hit that paralyzed New England Patriots wide receiver Darryl Stingley. They inked right-hander Troy Melton to a six-year contract extension that guarantees him $46.5 million with incentives and a club option for 2033 that could max out at $98 million over seven years. The hard-throwing right-hander will turn 26 years old in about two weeks. He has one year and 68 days of MLB service time currently, so this deal arrives as Melton was still five full seasons from free agency. Exchanging an extra year until free agency, and potentially two years if the Tigers use their club option, to guarantee himself at least $46.5 million is a pretty good deal for both sides. Melton wouldn’t have reached free agency until he was headed into his age 31 season, and with pitcher injuries being what they are, there’s always the risk that he wouldn’t be as valuable by that point in his career. From the Tigers’ perspective, they locked up six years of Melton at less than eight million a season, a bargain for a pitcher who is on track to be worth roughly 2 WAR per season if he continues on his current track. Of course, the Tigers, and no doubt Melton himself, expect continued improvements in the years ahead. With a 96-97 mph fastball with big extension that can reach triple digits, along with a deep and developing arsenal of pitches including a sinker, cutter, slider, curveball, and splitter, the potential here is pretty enormous.
